skill.name: awesome-bug-bounty
skill.description: Use when doing bug bounty hunting, vulnerability research, security report writing/analysis, payload or WAF-bypass selection, business logic / IDOR / race / API testing, recon methodology, tool choice (Burp vs Caido vs ZAP, AI pentest agents, MCP security testing, headless browsers), or looking up writeups/programs — e.g. "find XSS payload", "business logic checklist", "SSRF bypass", "HackerOne top reports", "bug bounty methodology", "which tools to install". Merges curated knowledge with source-repo fallbacks; authorized testing only.
skill.summary: Guides authorized bug bounty research with scoped methodology, payload references, tool selection, setup, verification, and reporting.
skill.author: yangtech-gh

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, documentation links, placeholders, and named environment variables. Confirmed risks include privileged host changes, active scanners, persistent configuration edits, unverified installers, and actionable payloads for cloud metadata, command execution, and sensitive file access. No prompt injection, obfuscation, or credential-exfiltration path was found.

remediation.issue: Actionable critical payloads can retrieve cloud metadata and host files.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization before presenting them, prefer detection-only probes, and separate destructive or credential-retrieval payloads behind a clear opt-in.

remediation.issue: Installation commands trust latest releases and third-party scripts without integrity checks.
remediation.suggestion: Pin commits or versions, verify checksums or signatures, and avoid piping downloads directly into interpreters or executable directories.

remediation.issue: The workspace stores privileged sessions without defined at-rest protections.
remediation.suggestion: Store session references in a credential manager, enforce restrictive permissions, redact exports, and define automatic cleanup after each engagement.

remediation.issue: Some active tools depend on prose scope rules instead of technical enforcement.
remediation.suggestion: Require a validated scope manifest, target allowlists, rate caps, and human confirmation before scans, exploitation, or privileged installation.

content.value_statement: Bug bounty research can become fragmented across tools, payloads, and reporting workflows. This skill organizes authorized testing into scoped, evidence-focused playbooks.
actual_capabilities: Routes common vulnerability classes to focused testing notes and payload references.
Builds a scoped reconnaissance workflow with deduplicated assets, endpoints, and findings.
Compares proxies, scanners, MCP servers, and agent-based security tools.
Provides installation and configuration guidance for referenced testing tools.
Structures evidence, severity reasoning, remediation, and bug bounty reports.
limitations: It does not grant permission to test any system or expand a program scope.
Payloads and commands require manual validation before use on production systems.
Third-party tools, repositories, and installation instructions may change after publication.
Automated findings still require human reproduction and program-specific severity review.

use_cases.title: Create a Scoped Hunt Plan
use_cases.description: Turn program rules into a phased reconnaissance and testing plan with rate limits and exclusions.

use_cases.title: Choose a Verification Workflow
use_cases.description: Select appropriate proxy, scanner, and replay tools for a suspected vulnerability class.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Reports
use_cases.description: Convert reproduced findings into consistent, evidence-focused reports with impact and remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Beginner Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe bug bounty plan for [authorized program]. Use the stated scope, exclusions, rate limits, and test window. Start with passive checks.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Testing Playbook
prompt_templates.prompt: For suspected [vulnerability type] on [in-scope feature], provide a non-destructive checklist, required evidence, stop conditions, and suitable tools.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Candidate Finding
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this authorized test result: [redacted evidence]. Identify missing controls, reproduction steps, likely impact, false-positive risks, and safe verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Surface Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a deduplicated workflow for [authorized program] covering web, API, authentication, and MCP surfaces. Include tool boundaries, rate caps, evidence gates, and reporting.

output_examples.input: Plan an authorized assessment for one web application and API with a strict request limit.
output: Scope manifest listing approved hosts, exclusions, test window, and request limits.
Passive asset discovery followed by rate-limited endpoint mapping.
Manual verification gates before intrusive tests or report submission.

output_examples.input: Turn a reproduced authorization issue into a concise bug bounty report.
output_examples.output: A report with affected endpoint, role comparison, redacted evidence, impact, severity rationale, reproduction steps, and server-side authorization guidance.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, exclusions, rate limits, and test windows before any active request.
Use minimal-impact proofs and stop when testing could change data, disrupt service, or expose unrelated users.
Redact credentials and personal data, then reproduce each finding before reporting it.
anti_patterns: Do not run scanners, payloads, or reconnaissance against targets outside the approved scope.
Do not execute unpinned installers or privileged commands without reviewing sources and obtaining confirmation.
Do not submit automated findings without stable reproduction, impact evidence, and duplicate checks.

faq.question: Does this skill authorize security testing?
faq.answer: No. You must have explicit permission and follow the program rules for every target.

faq.question: Can it run security tools?
faq.answer: It provides commands and MCP setup guidance, but execution should require user confirmation and validated scope.

faq.question: Does it guarantee a valid vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. Scanner output and hypotheses remain candidates until a human reproduces them with clear evidence.

faq.question: Can it help write reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a structure for evidence, impact, severity, reproduction, and remediation.

faq.question: Are cloud API keys required?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents local, deterministic, and no-key options for several workflows.

faq.question: Is every installation command safe to copy directly?
faq.answer: No. Review versions, integrity checks, privileges, destination paths, and upstream instructions before execution.
